command.usable_size: page_size-255..page_size (minimum 257); a prior resize may leave <480 and must reach the original next-call ordered refusal
command.logical_pager_page_count: 0..4294967295 from the same externally stabilized pager snapshot, not blindly physical file length
command.wal_ready: 0 or 1; true only after real WAL opening and page-one refresh

actions.1: accept header byte geometry; outer I/O/lock authority remains required
actions.2: open WAL successfully and reread page one before continuing
actions.3: apply requested page size successfully and reread page one before continuing
actions.4: format or page-count error: raw SQLite semantic code 26 NOTADB or 11 CORRUPT

return_status.256: complete semantic decision, including action=4 format error

order: Logical page count uses header nPage only when nonzero and change counters agree; reset_database produces the empty branch.
A nonempty view checks magic, marks future write format read-only, rejects read version>2.
WAL open/reread occurs before payload fractions or page-size admission; no_wal selects the original bypass.
Page-size reread occurs before declared-count overflow or usable-size<480 decisions.
Count overflow is CORRUPT before usable-size rejection unless writable_schema clamps it.
Only final acceptance publishes logical page count and payload limits.
compatibility_notes: Read/write version zero is not tightened beyond the retained lockBtree comparisons.
Unknown write versions>2 produce read-only metadata; unknown read versions>2 reject.
Empty/reset views do not inspect header magic or change vacuum metadata.
Resize proposals may have usable_size<480; the reread then rejects at the original ordered check.
This operation does not validate schema format or text encoding beyond what lockBtree itself checks.
Current usable_size below480 remains admissible as transport state after a resize; only the ordered nonempty semantic check rejects it. Empty/reset branch preserves original geometry.
not_implemented: actual WAL opening and pager page-size mutation or their error paths

arithmetic.division: Exact divide32 retained from the qualified SQLite selected-cell HIA core; no unsupported FloorDiv operation.
